why: willametteweek.com is Willamette Week's GENUINE FORMER domain — archived from 1998, serving WW's own assets, still 301-redirecting to wweek.com as late as 2020. It is NOT a composed hostname like clark.house.gov, and the earlier worklist framing that called it one was wrong.
But the five cited article paths never existed: zero Wayback captures of any URL containing "answer-our-questions" anywhere on wweek.com, and all five return HTTP 404 at the live real domain.

Decisively: the claimed CONTENT is absent from WW's real coverage of these races. The genuine Oct-16-2024 endorsement articles for Districts 1-4 and mayor contain ZERO mentions of immigration, sanctuary, ICE, rent control/regulation/stabilization, zoning, vouchers, or even the phrase "affordable housing" — the exact topics these rows assert (Local Immigration Enforcement for 9 of 12 politicians, Rent Regulation for 6, Affordable Housing for 11). So this is not a wrong address for real journalism; the journalism does not exist.
Person coverage is thin too: Sameer Kanal is not named in the D2 endorsement in any form; Koyama Lane and Loretta Smith get one mention each, Mitch Green two, Morillo and Dan Ryan three.
WW's only per-candidate format ("city council entrance interview") covers about six candidates total, two of ours, and also has zero immigration or zoning.
Every one of the 57 rows is SOLE-SOURCED to the fabricated URL — unlike the bilalmahmood case where 10 of 12 rows had a live co-source. There is nothing to re-point alongside.
